text:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] 02:12 UTC cost-routing: sudden shift -> highest-volume traffic routed to cheapest-variant (model: redwood/gpt-7b-quant-lite) with increased quality regressions observed. error-rate symptom: elevated complaint count, automated evals failing. paging sre_oncall_alex and prod-eng-kevin :rotating_light:

sre_oncall_alex: ack. I see the spike in the routing dashboard and a lot of 5xx-ish evaluation failures flagged by the quality-monitor job. Pulling logs now.

prod-eng-kevin: on it. Quick summary pls: is this a single-policy change or a broader config rollout?

ops_maria: I rolled a cost-sensitivity policy change yesterday (policy id: cost-tilt-v3) that lowers cost threshold for fallback to quantized variants during peak. It passed staging smoke but not the new eval set.

sre_oncall_alex: copying the traces. The smart-router shows a cascade: region fallback + cost policy -> route to cheapest variant in eu-west-1, then cross-region fallback to the same low-cost instance when primary saturated. That created a loop-like amplification.

prod-eng-kevin: ok stop the policy. Is there a kill-switch?

infra-sre-sam: I can disable cost-tilt-v3 from the control-plane now. Will run a targeted revert to cost-tilt-v2 which pins a min-quality threshold. Doing it in 2...1... (deploy-bot) 

deploy-bot: rollout revert started by infra-sre-sam at 02:16 UTC.

sre_oncall_alex: while revert is in progress, rate-limit the affected routing table to prevent further amplification. Can someone add an override to prefer last-good variant (redwood/gpt-7b-clean) until we validate?

prod-eng-kevin: adding pin rule now. CLI: 
```
redwood route update --policy cost-tilt-v2 --pin-variant redwood/gpt-7b-clean --scope customer-facing --reason "emergency pin after regressions"
```

prod-eng-kevin: pinned. Confirmed routing table shows ~78% traffic back to gpt-7b-clean in eu-west-1.

customer-success-anjali: getting inbound from two enterprise customers reporting summaries with hallucinations and truncated answers — one has elevated error rate in their dashboards. Not yet P0 but we should notify.

sre_oncall_alex: sam, can you validate that we aren't still auto-failing over to the quantized variant via region fallback?

infra-sre-sam: tracing cross-region failovers: the fallback chain had an ordering bug where cheaper-variant overrides explicit variant pins when capacity < 3. I've opened a quick fix to change the tie-breaker. Patch queued: change fallback precedence -> explicit pins > region fallback > cost-preference.

prod-eng-kevin: good. Patch diff: 
```diff
- precedence: [cost_preference, region_fallback, explicit_pin]
+ precedence: [explicit_pin, region_fallback, cost_preference]
```

prod-eng-kevin: deploying hotfix to control-plane now (no model re-deploy).

deploy-bot: hotfix deploy started at 02:23 UTC by prod-eng-kevin.

sre_oncall_alex: monitoring metrics: quality-eval failure rate trending down after pin; customer error reports still trickling. Keep throttles in place for 30m.

customer-success-anjali: raising an interim notification to affected customers: short note + postmortem promised in 24h. Draft: "We observed a rerouting to a lower-cost model variant that led to degraded output quality for some requests. We reverted the routing policy and pinned traffic to the previous model. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." OK to send?

prod-eng-kevin: yes go ahead. Include rough ETA: 4 hours for initial RCA, 24h for final.

customer-success-anjali: sent to 3 customers at 02:30 UTC. One replied asking about SLA and replay of requests — need ops for replay access.

sre_oncall_alex: on replays: we have request logs archived; we can re-run a sampling through the pinned model to quantify delta. kevin, can you run a batch eval (1000 samples) in dev env?

prod-eng-kevin: scheduling batch eval now. CLI: 
```
redwood eval run --samples 1000 --from logs/2026-03-15/02:00-02:20 --target-model redwood/gpt-7b-clean --compare redwood/gpt-7b-quant-lite --metrics bleu,exact_match,quality_score
```

prod-eng-kevin: eval started at 02:36 UTC. I'll post results when done.

infra-sre-sam: FYI I rolled back the region-fallback aggressiveness flag from 0.8 -> 0.95 to reduce cross-region fallbacks while the policy is re-evaluated.

sre_oncall_alex: handoff note for next oncall: incident mitigated (policy reverted + pin + tie-break fix in deploy), customer notifications sent. Keep monitoring routing_quality, customer complaints, and eval job completion. If quality metrics re-elevate, escalate to on-call pager.

prod-eng-kevin: eval results incoming: initial pass shows quality_score drop of ~14% on gpt-7b-quant-lite vs gpt-7b-clean; BLEU/EM also lower. I'll attach diff summary.

prod-eng-kevin: summary: cheap variant saves ~35% token cost but fails key correctness prompts (long-context summarization) consistently. Not safe for customer-facing routes.

customer-success-anjali: passing this to account leads for impacted customers. One asked for a timeline for durable fix for the policy.

prod-eng-kevin: plan: 1) rollback cost-tilt-v3 permanently from prod until it passes an expanded eval set; 2) add canary gating in control-plane that runs selected prompt sets pre-rollout; 3) add explicit variant-protection config for customer-facing/classified routes.

sre_oncall_alex: I'll mark incident as SEV-2 mitigated and create a follow-up ticket for SEV-1 if we see reoccurrence. Handoff to next oncall (ops_maria) at 03:05 UTC.

ops_maria: taking over. Noted actions and will coordinate the postmortem.

pagerduty-bot: Incident 2026-03-15T02:12Z (ID: INC-26742) status updated to "Mitigated" by sre_oncall_alex. Follow-up: RCA ticket created: INC-26742-RCA.

sre_oncall_alex: final notes for RCA: primary root cause = missing gating in cost-tilt-v3 rollout + fallback precedence bug; contributing = insufficient eval coverage for long-context summarization workload. Add mitigations: rollout canary, expanded eval corpus, explicit pin whitelist, alerting on sudden policy-driven variant shifts.

ops_maria: thanks team. I'll open the postmortem draft and tag stakeholders. Any other items before I close thread?

prod-eng-kevin: please schedule a meeting with model-ops and product to decide acceptable cost-quality tradeoffs and guardrails.

customer-success-anjali: will follow up with customers with the RCA and remediation plan.

incidents-bot: thread closed at 03:05 UTC (automated).
